_meta.indication: CRESEMBA is an azole antifungal indicated for patients 18 years of age and older for the treatment of invasive aspergillosis and the treatment of invasive mucormycosis.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 9766-CL-0104 (Trial 1), the pivotal invasive aspergillosis trial
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, active-controlled noninferiority trial
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, noninferiority trial comparing isavuconazonium sulfate to voriconazole with a pre-specified noninferiority margin of 10%; patients randomized 1:1.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients ≥18 years of age with proven, probable, or possible invasive fungal disease per EORTC/MSG 2008 criteria; patients with creatinine clearance <50 mL/min were excluded.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint was all-cause mortality through Day 42; key secondary endpoint was DRC-assessed overall response at end of treatment.
pivotal_trials.n: 527 patients enrolled; ITT population of 516 (258 in each treatment group).
pivotal_trials.result: In the ITT population, Day 42 all-cause mortality was 48/258 (18.6%) for isavuconazonium vs 52/258 (20.2%) for voriconazole; adjusted treatment difference -1.0 (95% CI -8.0, 5.9). As the upper bound of the 95% CI (ranging 5.9% to 8.2% across populations) was below the pre-specified NI margin of 10%, noninferiority was demonstrated.

nct_ctgov.title: Isavuconazole (BAL8557) for Primary Treatment of Invasive Aspergillosis

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Trial 9766-CL-0103 (Trial 2), an open-label Phase 3 trial in IFD caused by Aspergillus species in patients with renal impairment or caused by rare filamentous fungi (invasive mucormycosis was a subset).
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, multi-center, non-comparative single-arm trial; the dosing regimen was similar to that used in the Phase 3 trial in invasive aspergillosis; efficacy in mucormycosis assessed against historical controls.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with invasive fungal disease caused by Aspergillus in patients with renal impairment or by rare filamentous fungi; the mITT-Mucorales population comprised 37 patients with infection due to Mucorales only.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: DRC-assessed overall response was the protocol primary endpoint, but 42-day all-cause mortality was agreed by the Applicant and FDA as the most relevant primary endpoint to allow comparison with historical controls.
pivotal_trials.n: 149 patients enrolled; 146 received at least one dose (ITT); mITT-Mucorales population = 37.
pivotal_trials.result: In the mITT-Mucorales population, all-cause mortality at Day 42 was 38% and at Day 84 was 43%; 31% of patients were assessed as success (14% complete, 17% partial), compared with historical untreated mucormycosis mortality estimates up to 97%.

nct_ctgov.title: Isavuconazole in the Treatment of Renally Impaired Aspergillosis and Rare Fungi

key_safety: Across two clinical trials (403 patients), the most frequently reported adverse reactions were nausea (26%), vomiting (25%), diarrhea (22%), headache (17%), elevated liver chemistry tests (16%), hypokalemia (14%), constipation (13%), dyspnea (12%), cough (12%), peripheral edema (11%), and back pain (10%). Hepatic adverse drug reactions, infusion-related reactions, and hypersensitivity reactions are warnings in labeling.
target_moa: Isavuconazole, the active moiety of the prodrug isavuconazonium sulfate, inhibits the enzyme cytochrome P450 sterol 14 alpha-demethylase (CYP51), interfering with ergosterol synthesis; ergosterol depletion disrupts fungal membrane structure and function, inhibiting fungal growth.
modality: Small molecule (water-soluble triazole prodrug hydrolyzed to the active moiety isavuconazole).

rems.type: A REMS was determined not to be required; safety findings were considered adequately addressed in labeling.

advisory_committee.vote: The Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee met January 22, 2015. For invasive aspergillosis the committee voted Yes 11, No 0, Abstain 0; for invasive mucormycosis the committee voted Yes 8, No 2, Abstain 1.

citations.quote: Under the provisions of Generating Antibiotic Incentives Now (GAIN) [Title VIII of FDASIA], NDAs for products with a QIDP designation receive a priority review. As isavuconazonium sulfate has QIDP designation for the submitted indications, these NDAs received a priority review. These NDAs are eligible for five additional years of marketing exclusivity under GAIN.

summary.text: NDA 207500 was submitted by Astellas on July 8, 2014 for treatment of invasive aspergillosis and invasive mucormycosis. Isavuconazonium sulfate carried QIDP designation under GAIN, which granted priority review, and had orphan drug designation for both indications. Aspergillosis efficacy was shown in a randomized double-blind noninferiority trial versus voriconazole, while mucormycosis efficacy was supported by a single-arm open-label trial compared against historical controls; the drug was approved March 2015 as a standard (non-accelerated) approval.
